NERF Fortnite TS-R Super Soaker Water Blaster Toy, Blue This really seems like a match made in heaven. It is a mashup of two of our household's favorite things. Also, it is one of the best branded product line from Fortnite which has seemed to have a troubled branding the right products. But now they seem to have found the proper product licensing options.

OK, we did get this at a less than opportune time, 43 degrees and raining is not very conducive to water gun battles, but there was no keeping the kids from trying this out. And it is a decent water gun. It has range and accuracy and puts out an OK stream. It isn't breaking any records, but we were happy with it functionality and the pump action. I'm a little less than thrilled with the overall construction. I think more thought could go into it as well as more details and parts. It is basically just a few large molded pieces with a limited palette. Much could be done to improve the aesthetics, but the price point is pretty low so I guess you get what you pay for.

But this is easily five stars based on the boys reactions to it. Bring on the summer!
text_fidelity_b: NERF Fortnite TS-R Super Soaker Water Blaster Toy, Blue

text_fidelity_a: Lehoo Castle Gemstone Dig Kit, Dig Up 12 Real Gems and Crystals, Gem Digging Kit for Kids with Mining Tools, STEM Science Educational Toys, Gift for Boys Girls These are fun. The mask and the goggle are size too big and very loose/flimsy so we ended up not using any of the protective GEAR (you can't keep it on anyway) . The rocks were mostly square and they mostly stay in the middle of the brick, which was a little disappointing for me because I was hoping for a treasure hunting kind of experience but that does make it much easier for the kids. These can be very messy. My 3yo ended up with dust all over and some in his mouth. My 6yo had some around his cuff and pants. I do advise wearing an apron if your child is wearing nice clothes. I personally felt there's a lot of improvement that could be made, including the tool size, rock size and shape, rock distribution, make of the protective gear, and possibly at least some kind of warning for parents that it's a messy project, even better if they provide apron. VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park 5 stars for the toy itself. 0 stars for the directions - they are awful! The pictures are in blurry black and white, and the wording is confusing. It took me far too long to put together, but I was impressed by the finished product.

First of all - this is big! Look carefully at the specs on this toy to see if it will fit well (or dominate) your play space. The colors and designs are bright and cheerful, which I like. There are a few specific mechanical steps to make this work right with the car, and I worried that it would be too complicated for my 2yo granddaughter. (1) The arm needs to be clicked down into position, (2) you need to wind the car up the ramp (and the crank for that is tricky - if you let go just a little, it slides back to the bottom), then once the car slides down the ramp into the cradle you need to (3) release the arm for the catapult to launch down the second slide. Again - sounds complicated, right? But my granddaughter mastered it in no time! I was surprised and happy about that.

I was also very happy that she played with this over and over. She never seemed to get bored with it. The little car plays music and phrases as it goes along, and even when all the steps didn't go perfectly (ie: the car crashed), my granddaughter was amused. One quick note: some of the joints seem to come apart easily, and since toddlers are a little rough, we needed to keep an eye on this. Still, this will be a great toy that grows with our grandkids!
text_fidelity_b: VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park

The end result, similarly was unimpressive. There is not much to do with the brain after it is completed. It is inedible and not exactly a piece of art.  The scientific information is spare. It seems that the emphasis is more of a gross novelty and for that you could get a standard Halloween type brain gelatin mold like [[ASIN:B009S5SL90 Brain Gelatin Mold Standard]]. So if you want to really aggravate a zombie, this kit is the ticket. It's short lived fun with minimal educational value.

text_fidelity_a: Foxnovo Universal Tall Landing Gear Skid for DJI F450 F550 Sk480 Multirotor Quadcopter These legs are the perfect upgrade for the Syma X8C (white) if you're going to be using a different camera. The stock legs are just too short to allow you to mount any kind of adjustable camera rigging and GoPro type camera. You will need to do some drilling in these legs (and shave off the mounting alignment flange of the quad) to make them fit. But, it's worth it. This pic is of the same legs (black) on my Syma X8G (same body as the C, just a different color) and these legs on my Syma X8C. These legs give you the spread and stability you need, as well as the height. They're rigid, strong and don't weigh much more than the stock legs. I've seen some negative reviews regarding 'flimsiness'. I think that anyone should keep in mind the original configuration calls for bracing between the legs, in such a way that actually provides more structural integrity to each leg. Therefore, no bracing means less rigidity, the greater the chances of breakage. Having said that, I've been flying my Syma X8 quads with these for a while now. One of which was totaled. Seriously, the quad dropped like a rock from about 150 feet, crashing through trees and broke HARD. I had to do a total rebuild with new body, motor mounts, gears, etc.The only parts re-used were the control board and motors and the LEGS, which DID NOT BREAK!

GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'

text_fidelity_a: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi What kid doesn't like dinosaurs?  This is perfert for your boy or girl who is into dinosaurs.  I suppose it could be considered an educational toy, but probably only marginally so.  Who says educational toys can't be fun too?  This is especially nice for a kid interested in archeology.  Contains a block of plaster that has embedded into it "DNA" stickers and a glow in the dark dinosaur.  After the fun of digging out the dinosaur and stickers with the included digging tools and brush, they are left with a dinosaur model, so even though the digging fun is over after one time (if they do it all at once), there is something to show for it.  There are also two "augmented reality" (AR) play mats that are completed with the DNA stickers that have been "excavated".  The mats when used with a cell phone and an application from the App Store (for Apple phones) or the Google Play Store (for Androids) produces a 3D dinosaur, visible on the phone.  One problem with this is that it might not work with all cell phones.  It is supposed to work with MOST Apple devices (8.0 and above).  On Android phones the only devices tested are Google Nexus Series, Samsung Galaxy S5 and Samsung Galaxy Tab.  I didn't have a cell phone to test this on, but it seems like it still might be fun even if that part doesn't work.  It's just that you might not be able to use the full capability of the kit if your phone doesn't work with the application.  Also if you give this to a child of only 8 (the lower age limit on this), they may not yet have a cell and you may not want them to have one at that age.  Since this contains many small parts, it needs to be kept away from small children, as there is a choking hazard (box says no one under 3).  I would have loved a toy like this when I was a kid.  Just remember to put down a newspaper when they are working on the plaster block in order to collect all the plaster pieces that are chipped off as they excavate.  Pricing of the kit is very reasonable.  Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player I looked forward to playing this game, but was very disappointed. It sounds fun - each player rolls five dice and adds their roll to the roll of a common die. I thought it would be more like Yahtzee, but it was not nearly as fun as that classic game. The common die gives the chance for each player to double their score, which helps someone come from behind and catch up with the player that is leading. However, when rolling only 5 dice, the odds of getting a decent roll were slim. It was almost impossible to get anything more than a three of a kind, and that was hard to do. This made the game more frustrating than fun. I've never played the original Farkle, and we had to make some house rules because many portions of the instructions were unclear, which added to my frustration. The instructions referred to online video directions being available, but I didn't think it was worth having to watch a video to learn to play what should have been a very simple dice game.

For those familiar with Farkle, the common die may add an interesting twist, but the bubble-popper and dice risers are unnecessary. The bubble-popper for the common die does not roll the die well and seems like it would break after a few uses. We took the die out and rolled it by hand. This was much easier and kept the game moving more quickly. (On a side note, when we removed the die from the bubble-popper, it looked dirty!) The dice risers are rickety and make the play of the game more confusing. Since you can't combine the numbers you get on individual rolls, it's necessary to keep track of what you got on each roll within a round. It was impossible to do this on the risers, so we just started putting the dice aside from each roll and not using the risers at all.

The dice themselves are sturdy, even though the white coloring started coming off the numbers after only a couple of uses. I like that there are four sets in different colors so each player can have their own color. However, the red and orange were too similar in color and it was hard to tell them apart.

Overall, I think the dice risers and bubble-popper are flimsy and just a gimmick to make more out of the game than there is. It's not an exciting game and became very boring when it became clear it was too hard to get a decent score from an individual roll.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

Playin' Possum This is a great family friendly game that people of all ages can play. The concept is simple in that you need to just try to anticipate what others will play, sort of like rock-paper-scissors. But this game can have multiple players at a time and last until someone either collects enough winning cards (pieces of garbage) or is the last player standing.
The caveats are that you have the ability to "play it safe", which can avoid getting out if someone accuses you of trying to steal on your turn. This can lead to many rounds where nothing happens as someone needs to steal or accuse of stealing for the game to progress. It is also possible to start feeling repetitive after some time as the gameplay does not allow for much variation to keep it interesting. For what it is, it is a fun quick game that doesn't require a lot of setup or learning. But don't expect it to last a long time before people want to do something else instead.
text_fidelity_b: Playin' Possum

text_fidelity_a:
Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball I love geography and travel, and putting this together is both fun in a puzzle sort of way and great for reminiscing about past travels and dreaming about places yet to be seen in person. It's really cool - even cooler that it comes with a stand and you have a globe of your own afterward.

It is very up to date - it includes S. Sudan. And a warning to independence haters: Kosovo is shown as its own country. It is quite small and not labeled, but it has its own color.

We did the first half (the bottom) in the first night, but used the numbered backs as a guide as shown on the instruction sheet. It was fun, but left something to be desired. I wished they didn't have the numbers, and thought they would be impossible to ignore. After this, this was going to be the first Ravensburger puzzle I would have given less than five stars.

BUT the second night we finished it, but without the numbers. Turns out they were easy to ignore, and this allowed it to be what it should have been all along.

It might be overwhelming to not look at the numbers at first, but I suggest you do it that way. I suspect you still will have it done in 3-4 nights (assuming a few hours each night - it is addicting).

The pieces are plenty durable for snapping together, but many pieces are alike, so you could conceivably put the whole thing together as a sphere, but have it still be wrong. Anyone with any sense of geography would be able to catch a mistake like that. And when in doubt, the backs are numbered.

And when you're done, you have a nice little globe, textured to show it was a puzzle, and with a reasonably good looking stand. Very neat.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver) This is my first lightsaber in about a decade. The last one I owned what a Force FX by Hasbro; my, how technology has evolved.

This lightsaber is cheaper than the one I purchase, yet has a lot more to offer. While it doesn't have the "expanding" lights (it's sort of like a flashlight), the features it has make up for it. There's only one button, yet it does so much. Initial long press wakes it up or puts it to sleep. While it's on standby, there are button sequences that control music, volume, and sound font.

With the light emitted, the lightsaber has clash functionality, and the ability to change colors. What I love about changing colors is that the colors cycle in a rainbow fashion; there is no predetermined number of colors. See a color you like between cycles? Stop on it and it stays. Pretty nice.

The smooth swing works effectively, but the sound doesn't fade away; instead, there's an abrupt stop. So if you turn the lightsaber one way, the sound follows in synchronization, but immediately stops. It sort of takes away from the effect, but I imagine lightsabers with better smooth-swing functionality have better accuracy.

One day, while charging the lightsaber after a month, the charging sound came on and kept announcing the charging state. I was a little concerned, but left it. Suddenly, the sound was rapid, then silence. I checked the lightsaber and the charging light wasn't on. I tried different outlets, but no fix. Thankfully, the lightsaber is easy to disassemble, so I checked out the battery. It seems fine, but I am awaiting a new one to make sure it's just the battery that was fried.
text_fidelity_b: CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver)

Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder This version adds difficulty without making it more interesting. In this game, there are both railways and ship routes to build, which means you have to collect cards for each route in the correct color and mode of transportation. Effectively, this game adds twice the number of colors you have to collect to build things. In the original game, you always end up with a bunch of cards in your hand that aren't useful to you because they're not the colors you need to finish your tickets. This game is twice as bad in that regard. Furthermore, there are fewer ship cards, even though you're expected to build more ship routes than train routes. Many of the ship cards are actually worth 2 of that color, which theoretically allows you to collect fewer cards of that color before building, but what actually happens is that you can go through the entire stack of ship cards without getting what you need because the other players are unintentionally hoarding the few cards in the color and type you need.

I didn't hate this game, but I wouldn't play it again.
text_fidelity_b: Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder

I did end up putting this together and taking it apart about ten times before I was satisfied with it, so I definitely dumped more time than I intended into it. Making adjustments is often almost as big a job as starting from scratch. The loop at the top of the line was small, and that wanted to attach to a giant redwood, so I had to switch trees, though I'm sure I could've bought a longer section of cable. The bottom end seems like it would be able to handle a big tree fine. Maybe I could've swapped ends, but it doesn't indicate that as an option anywhere. The instructions are a bit sparse, but mostly sufficient. I hadn't realized initially that the big velcro pads had a slot for the cable to go through to keep it from slipping off the pad. By the time I got everything attached high enough, I had a lot of trouble pulling all of the slack out of the line. The turnbuckle was way too short for the task. I eventually had to get creative with clamps and bungee cords to get enough mechanical advantage to pull it tight enough to clamp it down.

The included seat is nice for when you want both adults and kids to be able to use it. It allows it to be attached up high enough to be out of the way and usable by adults, while still being low enough for smaller kids to ride on the seat. My kids use it more than the trampoline, so it's a hit.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Words with Friends Luxe I love word games and I particularly like Scrabble. I have seen Words with Friends online and though I have not played it online I suspected this game would be a lot like Scrabble. It definitely is. It's a good game and can be a great addition to family game night.

Words with Friends is a crossword game where the goal is to create words and score points by strategically placing the words on the game board. The board has a number of bonus squares where extra points can be had - double word, triple word, double letter and triple letter. The player with the highest score at the end of the game wins. Each player gets 7 letter tiles (with point counts printed directly on the tiles) with which to make words. Play continues until all the tiles are used and all of the scoring opportunities are expended.

Game play as described above is just like Scrabble, but there are some differences. The score assigned to individual letters varies is little bit. The bonus squares are laid out differently too. Using all 7 letters in one turn results in a 35-point bonus, not 50.

The tiles are a glassy-looking orange color and are very aesthetically pleasing, even though they are simply plastic. The board itself is a two-piece creation and it clips together into one larger board. Assembly is simple.

I noticed a couple of flaws in this game, though these are not enough to lower my opinion of the game enough to matter. First, the board does clip together and turns nicely - on hard, flat surfaces. On carpet, the board can be a little uncooperative and can come apart. My second complaint is that the rules are so general that there is a little room for interpretation. People who have played Scrabble have a slight advantage - the unspecified rules are easy to fill in.

I especially like something printed on the box: "Your Smart Phone Unlocks Digital Features (phone not included)" Sorry, this made me laugh - I hope it's clear to everyone that there's no phone in the box...

Other than a touchy board and some slightly incomplete rules, this is a very fun game and is sure to be a hit on game night. My teenager and I have been playing and he's learning that I know more than he thought I did...
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Words with Friends Luxe

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games UNO: Roboto Game I have to remember that we are living in a society that remakes or revamps everything....from movies (Planet of the Apes, Star Wars, Star Trek, etc) to television shows (Charlie's Angels), it was only a matter of time before they remade/revamped classic games that I grew up with (Uno, Monopoly, and Operation). And while I am still can't decide if that is a good thing or not, I do think that this version will appeal to most. While I can usually "trick" my 10 and 13 year old sons to play Classic Uno, I wondered would this version of the game appeal to them more because it has a computerized component. After all, the robot is cute with it's little voice, and the cards fit nicely in a holder on it's head. Especially because today's generation plays XBox, Nintendo, PSP, and the WII. I hoped that they would enjoy it especially on family night.

Surprisingly, this version was extremely interactive, entertaining and tons of fun....throwing out names and house rules, which provided a new twist to an already enjoyable game. The "new" additions to the Classic include: the ability to record the names of the players; the ability to add creative house rules where the last person to complete the task draws two cards; and the ability to add surprise commands. In other words, you can make this game as funny as you want.And while my kids initially thought it was lame, they have asked to play it several times creating silly rules and cute nicknames. I definitely think this game will appeal to some.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games UNO: Roboto Game

Overall the new tracks stay together very well and are easy to put together, but in all honesty my three-year-old sometimes has to bring these new style wood tracks to me to get them apart, which she never has to do with the tiny set of traditional tracks that grandma has at her house. What is nice is that you can attach the tracks from either direction, since both sides connect identically.

We have the busy island set, the farm set, cranky at the docks, the train station, and the huge Tidwell sheds station. All of these sets fit together beautifully and provide a lot of different play options for the kids. However, the main complaint I have had is that most of these sets have not come with enough tracks. Even the huge sets, come with just enough tracks to barely get it together if you are very careful and mindful with how you put things together.

The main advantage of a set like this animal park one, is that you get a whole lot of tracks and every piece in it can be used to connect all of the big and exciting things in those huge sets. My daughter also really loved the simplicity of this set, that she doesn't really have to think too hard about how it goes together, she can just wind and turn and connect things up without too much planning ahead.

Overall this set adds to the larger Thomas sets really nicely and is a great way of introducing a little more interest and a lot more tracks into the busy island set or another one of the bigger sets.

text_fidelity_a:
Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity It's not wide enough to make a scarf, not for most kids. There is very little yarn included. You will need worsted weight for this kit.

The last point leads into my main issue with this. It does not provide enough information. You know you need yarn, but yarn varies in weight from lace (even gossamer) to super bulky. These terms refer to how thick the yarn is. Buy too thin, and the project will look terrible. Buy too thick and the yarn won't fit into the weft holes. You need worsted weight, and the only reason I know this is I knit and I recognized the yarn. The kit doesn't tell you.

If you hit a knot in the yarn, as I did, you should not keep going. Cut at the end of the row (the instructions don't tell you this) then start on the right side again (the instructions don't tell you this) and whenever you stop or start, leave a tail long enough to weave in later (nothing about weaving in tails is covered -- you're just supposed to know how to do that).

If you want to do the purse, for example, cut 15 strands at 32 inches each (not explained) so that they turn into 16 inch strands when doubled. You can get away with cutting 16 inch and having them single stranded, but it isn't optimal, especially when you are tying pairs at the end. And maybe do it with a yarn not in this kit. They barely provide enough yarn in this kit, and no one wants their kid playing yarn chicken and getting upset. It's cheap yarn. Get a good amount.

When you start the yarn, it is shipped in a center pull ball. While the value of balls is explained a little (I suppose over leaving it in a loose skein or hank to tangle on itself) the concept of center pull isn't touched on. Dig into the ball and get the end inside. That way the ball stays still while you work.

You don't really need the tool to guide the yarn back and forth, but it should have come with a comb to push it down and keep it even, a trick especially hard when you move the piece along down the thread. That's perhaps the biggest design flaw in this. It tends to make the work uneven because it's slid and it leaves gaps where the next section starts. That can mostly be worked out by blocking the piece after (another technique not covered -- wet it, stretch it into the shape you want and even out the rows, and pin it down to dry.)

This is a great kit for someone who already knows a lot about yarn projects like crochet or knitting, or of course weaving. For a first yarn craft, a kid is going to need some help, ideally from someone who knows a lot about yarn projects.
text_fidelity_b: Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity

text_fidelity_a: LeapFrog Fridge Phonics Magnetic Letter Set, Pink I used LeapFrog Fridge Phonics when my children were little. It also played the ABC song when you pressed the music note. We also had the Word Whammer that let you spell three letter words. The magnets were interchangeable and increased learning fun. Since then, I've always purchased LeapFrog products for the wee ones in the family. When I saw LeapFrog now had an adorable bus, I had to have it for my niece. It comes with the 26 letters of the alphabet and does everything the original LeapFrog did plus has some extra bonuses. Instead of just singing the ABC song, Leap sings two additional songs. He also uses the letters to create words and puts it in a sentence. (It's almost like having the Fridge Phonics and Word Whammer in one.) So not only is your child learning their alphabet, they are also learning how letter sounds work together to create words and complete sentences. The only downside of this darling phonics bus is the size of the letters. They used to be much larger.

Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

text_fidelity_a:
Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This is a really great idea for a children's bank and the top part, the counter, works really well. Unfortunately, there are a number of things here that made it not really work for my family. At least not at this time.

First, with little children in the house, the top buttons get pressed accidentally or on purpose when they are not supposed to and so the count has not been correct for that reason. I almost would've preferred some other method of managing bills and kept this as a coin counter only so that you have the immediate feedback putting something in, seeing the number change, and knowing that it's accurate. This would not be an issue in households only with bigger kids who can control themselves from pushing buttons inappropriately, but definitely made it not workable in my house during these years.

Next, I really hoped that the cool top would have threads so that they could fit on a mason jar of any size, so while the little ones are tiny they can have a little chart, and as they grow older they can have a large jar, but unfortunately it does not work with any size mason jar – the sizing, the threads, and the lip that hangs over are all totally different.

Lastly, and this is my main issue, the cheap, foggy, and unattractive plastic container that holds all of the money is so lightweight and is angled weird so that if there are primarily bills with only a few coins in there, the whole thing gets really top-heavy and wants to tip over. My son primarily gets money through finding change on the ground and through getting dollars or 20s on his birthday or Christmas. So there are a few coins in there, sure, but mostly single bills sent from afar through the mail. Had they made the top interchangeable with Mason jars, this would have been an issue because I just would put the whole thing on nice glass mason jar, probably one of those colored blue, purple, or green ones that they've come out with in recent years. Alas, you're really stuck with just the plastic container that the lid fits on. This limits how long anybody would want to use something like this, because I think most teenagers have slightly better taste than to want some cheap plastic thing of a single specific size sitting in their bedroom.

That said, for a very specific age range and if you don't have smaller children around the house, this could work really well and be a very fun way of having kids learn about saving and making it rewarding.
text_fidelity_b: Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size

text_fidelity_a:
NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version
